overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by creating inaccurate and insufficient minutes of its March 4 meeting, but found no violation on the notice, 'tabled' wording, or timeliness issues.

allegations.summary: Council argued the first complaint was untimely; the AG found it was timely filed within 30 days of the minutes' approval.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the first complaint was timely filed with the Council on April 17, the 30th day following the date on which the minutes were approved.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 4 minutes inaccurately recorded item 9.13a as tabled by the mayor's motion, when it was a single-member hold.
allegations.key_passage: However, we do find the minutes inaccurate and insufficient where they state that Mayor Petty moved to table the matter when in fact he made no motion, and where they do not summarize the corresponding discussion.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that describing item 9.13a as 'tabled' in the minutes was improper, and that the item could not later be taken up under the Council's rules.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, for purposes of the Open Meeting Law, we do not find the minutes of the March 4 meeting to be insufficient where they refer to item 9.13a as having been “tabled.”

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the Council's handling of item 9.13a violated its own rules by allowing it to be discussed at a later meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As stated above, we do not review whether the Council complied with its own rules and so would not review whether, under those rules, the Council was allowed to discuss item 9.13a. at a later meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 25 notice was insufficiently specific because three DOJ-related topics were listed under a 'Tabled Items' heading.
allegations.key_passage: The fact that the three topics at issue here were included on the notice for the March 25 meeting would reasonably lead a member of the public to conclude that the Council anticipated discussing the topics during its March 25 meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 30 days of the letter, amend the minutes of the March 4 meeting to address the deficiencies discussed.
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law. Additionally, we order the Council, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to amend the minutes of its March 4 meeting to address the deficiencies discussed above.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
